opportunities.title: 24/7 intake-to-consultation agent with conflict screen and partner-approved booking
opportunities.problem: The firm has exactly two ways in: a phone line staffed Mon-Fri 9-5 and a Webflow form whose only routing is to the two partners' own inboxes. There is no online scheduling, no after-hours capture and no first-contact screening, so every inquiry that lands while a partner is in court, in a closing, or after 5pm waits until the next business day for a human to even triage it. For a two-attorney firm self-reporting 200+ matters a year, that delay sits directly on the revenue funnel.
evidence: Site states consultations are booked 'by calling our office or filling out the contact form', with no calendar, self-scheduling widget or booking tool anywhere on the attorney or contact pages: https://www.wileylavender.com/our-attorneys
Phone hours are listed as Mon-Fri 9AM-5PM, with no answering service, 24/7 line or after-hours coverage mentioned: https://www.wileylavender.com/contact-us

Contact form is a native Webflow form (required practice-area dropdown, Turnstile, /thank-you redirect) and the attorney bios publish individual partner mailto addresses, so inquiries are triaged by the partners rather than a central intake desk: https://www.wileylavender.com/contact-us

No Clio, Lawmatics, HubSpot, Calendly or other CRM/booking/marketing-automation script is loaded on the reviewed pages, even though Google Tag Manager (GTM-ML8VXZ7C) and GA4 are installed - analytics exists, lead routing does not: https://www.wileylavender.com/

O*NET lists screening calls, taking messages, routing to the right practice area and maintaining the attorney calendar as core legal-support tasks, and reports 54% of legal secretaries rate 'importance of repeating same tasks' as extremely important: https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/43-6012.00

Automated intake triage is demonstrated feasible at referral-service scale: an ensemble of small models plus auto-generated follow-up questions reached 97.37% hits@2 when routing 419 real queries (academic conference paper, JURIX 2025; arXiv preprint 2509.07170 - low-complexity screening setting, not a law-firm deployment): https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.07170
opportunities.agent_design: Two front doors into one agent. (1) Web: the existing form is replaced by a conversational intake that asks structured qualifying questions - matter type from the firm's own seven-option menu, county/venue, key dates and any limitation-period or return-date flag, opposing party name for a conflict screen, urgency and how they found the firm - then offers real consultation slots pulled from the two partners' M365/Google calendars. (2) Phone: an after-hours voice agent answers, captures the same structured record, and hands off a transcript plus summary; business-hours calls continue to ring the office. The agent writes a structured lead record (case-management system if one exists, otherwise a lightweight CRM/database with an audit log), opens a conflict-check request against a supplied party list, and books the consultation only when (a) no conflict hit and (b) either a default rule the partners pre-approve or a partner taps approve. Exceptions - conflict hit, urgent limitation date, personal-injury matter, out-of-scope work, existing client - are escalated to a named partner with a one-tap approve/decline. The agent never gives legal advice and states plainly that no attorney-client relationship exists until engagement. Client identifiers stay in a tenant-isolated, zero-retention environment under a DPA; transcripts are retained on the firm's terms.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A chatbot subscription cannot read two partners' calendars, cannot write a structured record into a case system that does not yet talk to the website, cannot run a conflict screen against a party list, and cannot hand a call and a web inquiry to the same case record. This needs persistent state across two channels, calendar and CRM integration, escalation logic with approvals, and a confidentiality-preserving deployment (client identity and matter facts are privileged under N.J. RPC 1.6), plus an audit trail for supervision (RPC 5.3). Reliability matters too: O*NET reports 50% of lawyers rate consequence of error as extremely serious, so an ungrounded general chatbot improvising intake answers is a liability, not a saving.

impact_estimate.range: Approximately 130-190 hours/year of partner-plus-support intake time recovered (roughly 2.5-3.5 hours/week), worth $3,900-$5,800/year valued at NJ legal-secretary pay and materially more where the recovered time is partner time; plus 15-40 additional booked consultations/year from after-hours and in-court-hour inquiries. New-matter fee revenue is deliberately excluded from the range because no fee or matter-value data is published.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes ~400-700 inquiries/year derived from the self-reported 200+ matters/year at 2-3 inquiries per retained matter (inference, unverified); assumes 25-35 minutes of human handling per inquiry today including phone tag and manual scheduling (inference); assumes 40-60% of that handling time is removed; values the time at the NJ legal-secretary median of $63,080/yr (~$30.33/hr) as a floor, noting partner time costs far more per hour but is not converted here; assumes after-hours and in-court-hour inquiries are currently deferred rather than captured by any other channel (inference from the absence of an answering service); the booked-consultation uplift assumes roughly 3-5% of currently deferred inquiries end in a booked consult once slots can be self-scheduled (inference, not measured).

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-4 weeks: replace the Webflow form with a structured conversational intake covering all seven practice areas; connect it to one source of truth for leads (case management if the firm has it, otherwise a hosted CRM/database); wire after-hours voice capture to the same record; enable booking into both partners' calendars with a partner-approval step on exceptions; run 20 live inquiries in shadow mode before going live; deliver a weekly dashboard of response time, qualification rate, booked-consult rate and after-hours capture. Conflicts remain human-decided, with the agent only flagging.

opportunities.title: Pleading and deadline agent: template-grounded drafting plus a conservative docket calendar for the volume practice
opportunities.problem: Two named attorneys report 200+ matters a year across matrimonial, landlord-tenant, consumer fraud, quiet title, debt collection, Chapter 7 and real estate closings - all document-heavy and deadline-driven - and no paralegal, case-management system, DMS or document-automation tooling appears anywhere in the firm's visible footprint or hiring signals. Caption blocks, discovery sets, collection complaints, service copies and docket entries therefore fall on the partners, and every one of those matters carries dates that cannot slip.
evidence: Home page self-reports 200+ successful cases per year and 1K+ clients (the Our History page says 5K+), while the attorneys page lists only two attorneys and states clients work 'directly with our partners' with 'no handoffs': https://www.wileylavender.com/our-attorneys

Pankaj Maknoor's practice list is high-volume and document-per-matter: landlord/tenant disputes, consumer fraud, quiet title actions, personal injury, debt collection and Chapter 7 bankruptcy: https://www.wileylavender.com/attorney-details/pankaj-maknoor

No case-management, document-management, e-signature or drafting tooling is loaded on the site - only Webflow, GTM/GA4 and Cloudflare Turnstile - and no client portal or document upload is advertised: https://www.wileylavender.com/contact-us

No careers page exists (/careers returns 404) and SimplyHired shows zero listings for the firm name, consistent with there being no paralegal or legal-secretary bench to absorb drafting volume: https://www.simplyhired.com/search?q=%22Wiley+Lavender%22

O*NET lists preparing, proofreading and processing summonses, subpoenas, complaints, motions and pretrial agreements, and organizing case files and exhibit sets, as core legal-secretary tasks: https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/43-6012.00

Citation risk is measured, not hypothetical: in a peer-reviewed study (Journal of Legal Analysis 16(1), 2024) ChatGPT-4 produced legal hallucinations on about 58% of verifiable questions about random federal cases and Llama 2 about 88%: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.01301

Even legal-specific retrieval tools hallucinate: a preregistered evaluation (academic working paper, Stanford legal informatics, arXiv 2405.20362) found Lexis+ AI and Westlaw AI-Assisted Research hallucinating 17-33% of the time: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.20362
opportunities.agent_design: A drafting agent restricted to repetitive, structurally predictable documents, plus a separate deterministic calendaring service. Drafting: a template library per matter type (NJ caption block, landlord-tenant complaint and notice package, collection complaint, discovery requests/responses, divorce case information statement scaffolding, bankruptcy document checklist) that the agent fills from a structured matter record, retrieves supporting language only from the firm's own precedent files and approved sources, and outputs a Word draft with every authority it cites flagged and linked - no authority is inserted without a retrieved source. A blocking verification step (citation check plus a required partner sign-off in track changes) means nothing leaves the office unreviewed. Calendaring: a rules table, not a language model, computes dates (limitation periods, motion return dates, eCourts cutoffs, service deadlines), writes them to a shared calendar with two-touch escalation (7 days and 48 hours), and requires a human to confirm any date it derives from a document. Every generated draft stores who generated it, which precedent it used and which attorney approved it, satisfying supervision and audit expectations. Client files stay in a private/tenant-isolated environment with zero training on firm data.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This is the one area where off-the-shelf assistance is measurably unsafe: 58% hallucination on case-specific questions in a peer-reviewed study and 17-33% in legal-specific retrieval tools means a generic assistant will eventually fabricate authority into a filing. Getting this usable requires retrieval grounded in the firm's own templates, a hard citation-verification gate, deterministic date arithmetic kept outside the model, and an approval audit trail - i.e. integration with Word, the firm's file store and its calendar, under a DPA that satisfies privilege. O*NET also reports 60% of lawyers rate being exact or accurate as extremely important, which rules out autonomous filing.

impact_estimate.range: Approximately 110-190 hours/year of document-preparation and docket-entry time removed (roughly 2-4 hours/week), worth $3,300-$5,800/year at NJ legal-secretary median pay; the larger, unquantified value is avoided deadline misses and write-downs, plus capacity for additional matters without adding staff. Modest direct savings - this opportunity is bought for risk and capacity, not for headcount reduction.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes 200 matters/year (self-reported and unverified) at 2-4 documents each needing caption/format/proof and a docket entry (inference); assumes 1.5-2.5 hours of support-equivalent effort per matter on those steps; assumes 25-40% of that effort is removed, with the partner review step retained and therefore not counted as a saving; values hours at the NJ legal-secretary median $63,080/yr (~$30.33/hr) rather than at lawyer rates; assumes no paralegal is currently employed, which is unverified - if support staff exist, the saving lands as redeployed capacity rather than recovered dollars.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-4 weeks, single matter type: build the template plus retrieval drafting agent for one high-volume document (landlord-tenant complaint and notice package, or an uncontested divorce document set) and the rules-based deadline calculator for that same matter type wired into a shared calendar. Deliver: Word output with verification checklist, 20 real drafts produced and partner-reviewed, measured drafting minutes per document against a pre-pilot baseline, and a written escalation/approval protocol. No e-filing automation in the pilot.

opportunities.title: Matter portal with document-collection and status-update agent for divorce, bankruptcy and estate files
opportunities.problem: There is no client portal, no document upload, no payment link and no status page - the only self-service path a client has is a message box that lands in a partner's inbox. Meanwhile the practice mix (matrimonial, Chapter 7, estate administration, debt collection) is exactly the kind that stalls on client-supplied documents and repeated 'where are we?' questions, and the firm markets responsiveness, transparency and no hidden fees as its core values, which signals that slow replies and billing surprises are the anxieties it is fighting.
evidence: No client portal, document upload or payment link is advertised anywhere on the site; the only self-service path is the message form: https://www.wileylavender.com/contact-us

Stated core values are responsiveness, transparency and personal partnership, and the firm-curated testimonials on the home page praise responsiveness, transparent fees and direct partner access - self-published marketing, not independent reviews, but it shows where the firm believes it is judged: https://www.wileylavender.com/

The matter mix is document-gathering heavy: matrimonial (financial affidavits, discovery), Chapter 7 bankruptcy (schedules, pay stubs, tax returns, creditor lists), estate administration and debt collection: https://www.wileylavender.com/attorney-details/pankaj-maknoor

After-hours coverage does not exist - phone hours are weekday 9-5 only - so a client who wants to send a document or ask a status question at 8pm has no channel at all: https://www.wileylavender.com/contact-us
Practices span the full document-gathering range from matrimonial to estate planning/administration and real estate closings, per the site's own service menu: https://www.wileylavender.com/contact-us
opportunities.agent_design: A lightweight, access-controlled matter portal (per-matter permissions, M365/SharePoint or S3-backed storage under the firm's existing tenancy) that a client reaches with a one-time link rather than a password reset loop. On matter opening, the agent generates a document request checklist from a per-matter-type template (e.g. Chapter 7: pay stubs, two years of returns, creditor list, ID; divorce: financial affidavit, discovery responses, service proof) and tracks completion state. It sends scheduled reminders in the firm's name, acknowledges each upload, flags missing or unreadable files, and files documents into the matter folder with naming conventions applied. A second agent drafts plain-language status updates from the attorney's own case notes - never inventing progress - and queues them for partner approval before sending; fee/trust questions route to a human. Payment is a trust-compliant processor link surfaced per matter. Anything substantive, and any message touching strategy, is blocked behind attorney approval, with the full outbound log retained.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A chat widget cannot host authenticated, per-matter document storage, cannot enforce access control between opposing clients in the same firm, and cannot track which checklist items are outstanding across 200 matters. Doing this safely means identity and permissions, encrypted storage inside the firm's tenancy, integration with email, calendar and billing, and an approval gate on anything substantive - family-law and bankruptcy files are among the most sensitive personal records a small firm holds, so consumer-grade tools and consumer LLM endpoints are out. It also needs an audit log for supervision under RPC 5.3.

impact_estimate.range: Approximately 65-130 hours/year of client-chasing and status-reply time removed (roughly 1.5-2.5 hours/week), worth $2,000-$3,900/year at NJ legal-secretary median pay, plus faster document completion that shortens matter cycle time (unquantified here); it also reduces the after-hours silence that the firm's own positioning says clients punish.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes 12-20% of current client-facing administrative time goes to document chasing and status replies (inference - no time records or staff data available); assumes ~3-5 hours/week of such work across 200 matters/year; assumes 40-50% of it is removed with reminders and self-service uploads; values hours at the NJ legal-secretary median $63,080/yr (~$30.33/hr); assumes no client portal or document-upload tool already exists off-site, which matches the public tech footprint but cannot be confirmed.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-4 weeks on one matter type: stand up the portal for 10-15 Chapter 7 or matrimonial matters, with a per-matter document checklist, reminder cadence, upload acknowledgement and a partner-approved status-update template set. Deliver: working portal, checklist completion dashboard, reminder schedule, an approval-queue UI for outbound messages, and measured change in time-to-complete-document-set on the pilot matters versus a small comparison group.

lead_score.rationale: Pain (22/30): three independent, directly cited operational gaps - single-channel 9-5 intake with no booking, no case-management or drafting tooling against 200+ self-reported matters a year, and no client portal or document capture - all visible in the live site's own architecture. Capped below 25 because no independent reviews, complaint data, financials or headcount could be verified (Google Business Profile, Yelp, BBB, Avvo, Martindale and Super Lawyers were blocked), so 'this hurts' is inferred from how the firm operates, not from clients saying so. Fit (18/20): the work is squarely in A (intake/booking), C (template-grounded drafting) and D (portal plus form-to-CRM-to-calendar integrations); no hardware needed, and a natural path into an F retainer once intake and the portal are live. Ability to pay (13/20): two named partners, and lawyers are high earners statewide (NJ median $161,430 per the industry brief), but this is a two-person firm with no published revenue, and small-firm cash flow plus the cost of its own December 2025 website rebuild limits budget headroom. Ease of pilot (11/15): one co-founder can say yes and the organisation is small enough to deploy in weeks, but partner hours are the scarcest resource, the confidentiality review (RPC 1.6, 5.3) will slow the first deployment, and the absence of any case-management system means the pilot must also supply the system of record. Strategic (13/15): the intake-plus-docket-plus-portal stack is repeatable across the many two-to-five attorney NJ firms with this profile, and each of the three parts can be sold standalone.

best_evidence_signal: Consultations are booked only by phone (Mon-Fri 9-5) or a contact form that routes straight to the two partners' individual inboxes - no scheduling tool, no CRM, no after-hours capture anywhere on the site: https://www.wileylavender.com/our-attorneys
